title: Match Android refresh rate to PS2 output
summary: Hold emulation speed and scene constant, compare available Android refresh modes, observe cadence rather than raw FPS, and retain the most stable display policy.
heroAlt: PCSX2 on-screen performance display used to compare frame cadence while Android refresh modes change

sourceLabels.android-frame-pacing: Android display synchronization and frame-pacing concepts

blocks.text: Hold game speed constant before comparing display modes
Compare stable Android display modes against the effective PS2 output cadence without confusing refresh rate, emulation speed, and frame pacing.
Forcing the highest refresh rate cannot repair an emulator running below full speed and may add a different cadence or power cost.

items: Game region and expected output behavior recorded.
Emulation holds full speed in the selected scene.
Android automatic and fixed refresh choices documented.

blocks.text: Compare one stable refresh mode at a time

items: 1. Select a long camera pan or scrolling background and record the baseline mode.
2. Confirm emulation speed stays full throughout the observation.
3. Run the scene at the first supported fixed refresh rate.
4. Repeat at the next supported mode without changing renderer or resolution.
5. Look for regular repeated-frame cadence rather than a single FPS number.
6. Test touch or controller response without changing its connection.
7. Run long enough to expose thermal downshift or automatic mode switching.
8. Choose the stable mode with the best cadence and document its power tradeoff.

blocks.text: Refresh rate describes display opportunities; frame pacing describes when frames arrive; emulation speed describes how fast the PS2 workload advances.
The selected Android mode provides the smoothest repeatable cadence at full emulation speed without unstable switching or unnecessary thermal load.

items: Game speed stays constant across refresh comparisons.
The chosen mode avoids irregular bursts or visible mode switching.
A sustained pass preserves cadence and acceptable temperature.
Judder begins when speed drops: solve performance first.
Only an external screen stutters: inspect its mode and processing.
Automatic mode changes mid-scene: test a supported fixed rate.
A higher rate increases heat without smoother cadence: return to the lower stable mode.

blocks.text: Restore the original Android display policy
Return Android to its recorded automatic or previous fixed refresh mode.
PS2 titles do not all produce identical cadence
Region, interlacing, game engine, and cutscenes can change effective output, so one phone setting may not be ideal for every title.
